themes_detail.label: Explosive Graffiti Surge
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 17 two weeks ago—an 871% increase over the 8-week baseline of 1.8 complaints per week—suggesting a coordinated tagging campaign or breakdown in sanitation enforcement across CD 405.
evidence: 17 graffiti complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 1.8 average weekly complaints over prior 8 weeks (871% spike)
Z-score of 8.23 indicates statistically extreme deviation from baseline
No follow-up data showing whether spike has continued or resolved this week
reporting_angles: Map the geographic concentration of recent graffiti reports—is one neighborhood or corridor being targeted?
Interview DSNY about response times and staffing on graffiti removal crews; check whether the spike has triggered additional patrols

themes_detail.label: Tree Overgrowth Risk Spike
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints jumped to 15 THIS WEEK—a 145% increase above the 8-week average of 6.1 weekly complaints—raising concerns about blocked sidewalks, hazardous branches, and visibility at intersections.
evidence: 15 complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 6.1 average weekly complaints over prior 8 weeks (145% increase)
Z-score of 6.51 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Spring/early summer timing correlates with rapid tree growth; may reflect seasonal pattern or maintenance backlog
reporting_angles: Cross-reference this week's tree complaints with Parks Department maintenance schedules—are crews behind on pruning?
Document safety concerns: Are overgrown branches blocking sight lines at intersections or creating pedestrian hazards?

themes_detail.label: Day Care Complaint Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Day care facility complaints surged to 4 last week—a 700% spike above the 0.5 weekly average over 8 weeks—indicating possible health/safety violations, staffing issues, or enforcement gaps in an understudied part of the neighborhood.
evidence: 4 complaints filed last week vs. 0.5 average weekly complaints over prior 8 weeks (700% spike)
Z-score of 4.95 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Community board has repeated budget requests for child welfare and foster care support, suggesting chronic capacity issues
reporting_angles: FOIL the specific day care complaints to identify common violations (licensing, staffing, health code)
Investigate whether this reflects a real compliance problem or newly aggressive reporting by parents or inspectors

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Disturbances Rise
themes_detail.summary: Park-related noise complaints jumped to 11 two weeks ago—a 450% increase over the 2.0 weekly baseline—suggesting intensifying recreational conflicts or outdoor gatherings in CD 405 parks.
evidence: 11 park noise complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 2.0 average weekly complaints over prior 8 weeks (450% spike)
Z-score of 4.13 indicates statistically significant deviation
Community board has repeated requests for park reconstruction/upgrades; spike may indicate parks at capacity or lacking amenities
reporting_angles: Identify which parks are generating complaints—Fresh Pond Park, Ridgewood Reservoir, others?
Interview Parks Department about peak usage times and whether programming or enforcement capacity is adequate

themes_detail.label: Electrical System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints tripled to 5 two weeks ago—a 300% increase above the 1.2 weekly baseline—suggesting potential power infrastructure stress or aging wiring problems in buildings across the district.
evidence: 5 electrical complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 1.2 average weekly complaints over prior 8 weeks (300% spike)
Z-score of 5.67 indicates statistically extreme deviation
DOB data shows 444 alteration filings in past 90 days—many may involve electrical upgrades or remediation
reporting_angles: Cross-check electrical complaints against DOB violations and permits—are older buildings undergoing necessary upgrades?
Interview Con Edison about grid stress or outages in Ridgewood/Glendale during the spike period
